title: Deep learning detects acute pancreatitis on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT
summary: A convolutional network using arterial and portal venous phase CT from 552 patients at two university centers reached an AUROC of 0.89 and F1 of 0.83 on an internal hold-out set (n=116). On an independent external cohort of 95 patients it reached an AUROC of 0.99 (0.96-1.00) and F1 of 0.92. The study is retrospective, the control group were patients with suspected pancreatitis, and the authors call for prospective validation.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network classifier on monophasic and biphasic contrast-enhanced CT, with ensembling for biphasic studies

evidence.tested: Patient-level internal hold-out test (n=116) and independent external cohort (n=95); retrospective data.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance and clinical impact, and whether the very high external AUROC holds in larger cohorts; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Image-based detection of acute pancreatitis on CT.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
